financials.source: Form 990 FY2024 (calendar year ending Dec 2024) for Hackensack Meridian Health Inc-Subordinates, EIN 01-0649794, via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer. This is the group return with subordinates; the consolidated audited financial statements (filed with EMMA via NJHCFFA) show higher total assets (~$10.1B at Q1 2023) because they consolidate additional entities. Operating income is not separable from the 990 excess-of-revenue-over-expenses figure, which includes investment gains and other non-operating items. FY2022 operating income was $97.5M on $6.8B revenue per Becker's. Monthly NJ DHSS metrics showed 3.1% operating margin in April 2023. System targets 5% operating margin for FY2025. FY ends December 31.

balanceSheetWealth.investmentPortfolioSource: HMH Q1 2023 unaudited consolidated financial statements: current investments and assets limited as to use $1,147,254,000 + non-current investments and assets limited as to use $3,173,056,000 = $4,320,310,000 at March 31, 2023. Institutional Investor reported CIO Donna Snider oversees a $6 billion balance sheet. MarketBeat 13F filing shows $902.81M in publicly traded U.S. equity/ETF holdings as of June 30, 2025. The $4.3B figure is the most conservative verifiable number from official filings; the $6B press figure may include pension assets and other categories.

balanceSheetWealth.notes: Hackensack Meridian Health operates 18 hospitals including flagship Hackensack University Medical Center, Jersey Shore University Medical Center, and JFK University Medical Center. The consolidated balance sheet (Q1 2023 unaudited) showed total assets of $10,137,843,000, significantly higher than the $7.6B reported on the FY2024 Form 990 group return, because the audited statements consolidate additional entities. The Hackensack Meridian Health Defined Benefit Plan holds approximately $1.5B in pension fund assets per Institutional Investor.

communityBenefit.lownInstituteRanking: Largest fair share surplus in the nation; #1 health system nationally
communityBenefit.charityCarePolicyThreshold: 100% free care at or below 200% FPL; sliding scale above; insured patients with out-of-pocket exceeding 30% of gross annual income
communityBenefit.source: Community benefit total of $255.1M and charity care of $158.1M from HMH 2017 Community Benefit Report. Current-year Schedule H amounts not located in web search. Lown Institute 2024 report: HMH had largest fair share surplus in the nation at $358M, meaning community investment spending exceeded value of tax exemption by that amount. Nine HMH hospitals earned Top Hospital for Fair Share Spending designation. Hackensack UMC alone had $96.3M fair share amount. Note: AHA disputes Lown methodology as selectively excluding Medicare/Medicaid underpayments. Charity care policy thresholds from CareRoute.ai (unverified third-party source). NJ charity care partially funded via state Charity Care Subsidy Program per N.J.S.A. 26:2H-18.

taxAdvantage.notes: Hackensack Meridian Health operates 18 hospitals and 500+ care locations across New Jersey, all property-tax-exempt. NJ has a 9% corporate business tax rate (11.5% surcharge for income over $1M). Bond debt is issued through the NJ Health Care Facilities Financing Authority generating substantial tax-exempt interest subsidies. Multiple HMH hospitals qualify as DSH for 340B program participation. NJ has a 6.625% sales and use tax from which HMH is exempt on qualifying purchases.

ratios.investmentsToOperatingIncomeInterpretati: Cannot reliably compute — investment portfolio ($4.3B) is from Q1 2023 consolidated statements while operating income is not separable from Form 990 excess-of-revenue figure. Using FY2022 operating income of $97.5M as a reference: $4.3B / $97.5M = 44.1x, meaning the system held roughly 44 years of operating income in investments. However, these are from different fiscal years.
ratios.excessRevenueToTotalRevenueInterpretatio: FY2024 excess of revenue over expenses ($534.7M) as percentage of total revenue ($8.85B) = 6.0%. This is NOT operating margin — it includes investment gains and non-operating items. Operating margin was 3.1% as of April 2023 per NJ DHSS metrics.
ratios.bondDebtToCommunityBenefitInterpretation: Cannot reliably compute — bond debt ($3.05B) is from Q1 2023 and community benefit ($255.1M) is from 2017. Using those figures provisionally: $3.05B / $255.1M = 11.9x, meaning bond debt was roughly 12 times annual claimed community benefit. Both figures are dated.
ratios.charityCareVsStateInterpretation: Lown Institute found HMH had the largest fair share surplus in the nation ($358M), meaning community investment exceeded the value of tax exemption. Nine HMH hospitals in top 20% nationally. This suggests HMH exceeds NJ state averages, but specific charity care percentage vs. state average not computed.

accusation: Hackensack Meridian Health — the largest health system in New Jersey with $8.85 billion in revenue (FY2024), operating 18 hospitals under tax-exempt 501(c)(3) status, holding an investment portfolio of at least $4.3 billion, carrying approximately $3.05 billion in bond debt issued through the NJ Health Care Facilities Financing Authority, and paying CEO Robert C. Garrett $13.5 million in total compensation (FY2024, up from $7.8M the prior year) — serves as the Official Healthcare Partner of the New York Giants. The system laid off 1,043 workers across three WARN Act filings between 2020 and 2023, while Garrett's retirement package includes a CEO Emeritus role for up to one year. The 2021 renaming of MetLife Stadium's Legacy Club to the Hackensack Meridian Health Legacy Club illustrates the scale of the system's sports-marketing spend. HMH claims $255.1 million in community benefits (2017 figure; current amount not disclosed) and the Lown Institute found a $358 million fair share surplus, yet specific current-year charity care spending and its ratio to the value of tax exemptions remain unverified in public filings.
